faqs.question: How many words should a 2-minute Diwali speech have?
faqs.answer: About 200 words for a child in Classes 5 to 8. Median pupils read aloud 97 words correct a minute in mid-Grade 3 and 133 in mid-Grade 5 (Hasbrouck and Tindal, 2017), and stage pauses slow a speaker further. A senior student or adult at the 162-word adult median would need roughly 320 words for the same slot.

faqs.question: How do I start a Diwali speech at a school assembly?
faqs.answer: Greet the Principal, teachers and friends, give your name and class, then say the date: Diwali is on Friday, 29 October 2027. A concrete date in the second sentence settles a nervous speaker faster than a general line about lights.

faqs.question: What length suits a Class 1 or Class 2 child?
faqs.answer: Keep it near 50 words. In the 2017 norms, Grade 1 pupils read a median of 29 words correct a minute mid-year and Grade 2 pupils 84, so a full 100-word speech is a stretch. The first two paragraphs of the one-minute speech above come to 47 words, and the 40-word Hindi speech also fits.

faqs.question: What day of the week is Diwali in 2027?
faqs.answer: A Friday: Drik Panchang's New Delhi calendar puts Lakshmi Puja on 29 October 2027. Dhanteras opens the festival two days earlier, on Wednesday 27 October, and Bhai Dooj closes it on Sunday 31 October. For Tamil Deepavali, Drik Panchang gives Thursday 28 October.

faqs.question: Can my child give the speech in Hindi instead?
faqs.answer: Yes. The 40-word Hindi speech on this page takes about 25 seconds, and it comes with a transliteration and English gloss so you can check every word. Time it aloud once, because the reading-rate studies used here measured English and Dutch, not Hindi.

faqs.question: Should a child memorise the speech or read it from paper?
faqs.answer: Memorise it, but carry a cue card with the first three words of each paragraph. The mind going blank is among the most common fears in public speaking, reported in Kahlon and colleagues' 2019 study, and four to seven cues are enough to restart.

faqs.question: My child freezes on stage. What actually helps?
faqs.answer: Practice in front of real people helps more than reading alone. In a 2019 trial, 27 adolescents aged 13 to 16 did one 90-minute session of speech practice before a virtual classroom and their anxiety stayed lower three months later. If the fear is severe or lasts for months, speak to the school counsellor.

faqs.question: Is it okay to mention Jain and Sikh traditions in a Diwali speech?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it makes the speech more accurate. In Jain tradition the night recalls Mahavira's nirvana, and Sikhs observe Bandi Chhor Divas for Guru Hargobind's freedom from Gwalior Fort. Both longer speeches here give each tradition one line.

faqs.question: Can I use these speeches for an inter-school competition?
faqs.answer: They are original to this page, so there is no copied text in them, but check the competition's rules on outside help first. Judges remember a personal detail, so replace one sentence with something from your own family's Diwali.

faqs.question: Can a grandparent who missed the assembly still hear the speech?
faqs.answer: Yes, if you record it. SubhSandesh's Dedication page lets them find your station through radio static and hear your recorded voice introduce a song, so a short recorded greeting fits there. SubhSandesh does not write or time speeches; its pages are personal greetings made for one person.

# Diwali Speech for Students, Class by Class, Word-Counted

A Diwali speech for a school assembly needs about 100 words for every minute on stage, so a one-minute speech is roughly 100 words, a two-minute speech 200 and a three-minute speech 300. For scale, the median letter on SubhSandesh's miss-you pages is 88 words (n = 214 since July 2026), shorter than even the one-minute speech. Festival preparation also runs late: SubhSandesh's Raksha Bandhan 2026 figures, the closest festival analogue we have measured (n = 89), show 49.4% of pages made on the day itself and 27.0% on the eve.

Below are three original English speeches, one per class band and exactly counted, plus a short Hindi speech. Then come the 2027 dates they quote and stage-fear tips.

## How long is a Diwali speech, and why 100 words a minute?

A Diwali speech is a short assembly talk that greets the audience, explains what the festival marks and ends on a wish. Its length is set by the time slot and the speaker's pace.

In the [2017 oral reading fluency norms by Hasbrouck and Tindal](https://files.eric.ed.gov/fulltext/ED594994.pdf), the median pupil reads 97 words correct per minute in mid-Grade 3 and 133 in mid-Grade 5. They are American pupils reading fresh text, so treat this as a guide.

In [Brysbaert and Vantieghem's 2023 study](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC10360968), 94 Dutch-speaking adults read aloud at a median of 162 words a minute. A child pausing for breath sits well below that, so 100 is the safer figure; on 22 October 2026, one top-five India sample labelled "two minutes" ran to 94 words.

## Three original Diwali speeches in English, by class

Choose by the speaker's class: each length follows that age group's reading pace. Replace the bracketed name and class.

### 1. Classes 1 to 4, primary assembly: 100 words, one minute

At the mid-Grade 3 median of 97 words a minute, this takes about 60 seconds. It covers the date, the word and one story.

> Good morning, respected Principal, teachers and my dear friends. My name is [name], and I study in Class [class].

> This year Diwali is on Friday, 29 October 2027. Its other name, Deepavali, describes a line of lamps, which is exactly what all our balconies become that night.

> Long ago, the people of Ayodhya lit lamps to welcome Lord Rama home after fourteen years in the forest. We light them to say that darkness never gets the last word.

> This Diwali, let us share our sweets, keep the night gentle for animals, and smile at everyone. Happy Diwali, and thank you!

### 2. Classes 5 to 8, middle-school assembly: 200 words, two minutes

The mid-Grade 5 median is 133, but stage pauses slow speakers, so this fills about two minutes. It covers all five days.

> Good morning to our respected Principal, our teachers and all my dear friends. Today I want to talk about Diwali, not as one night, but as five days.

> In 2027 the festival begins with Dhanteras on Wednesday, 27 October, when families clean their homes and bring home something new. Thursday, 28 October, is Choti Diwali, or Naraka Chaturdashi, when Lord Krishna is remembered for defeating the demon Narakasura.

> The big night is Friday, 29 October: Lakshmi Puja, held under no moon. The darkest night of the month is the one we fill with the most light, and I think that is the cleverest idea in the whole festival.

> Then Saturday, 30 October, is Govardhan Puja, when Krishna is remembered for lifting a hill to shelter the people of Gokul from the rain. Sunday, 31 October, is Bhai Dooj, a day for brothers and sisters.

> Diwali also belongs to more people than we sometimes remember. Jains honour Lord Mahavira's nirvana, and Sikhs keep Bandi Chhor Divas, the very day Guru Hargobind walked free from Gwalior Fort.

> So this year, let us light one extra diya for someone who is spending the festival alone, far from family. Happy Diwali, and thank you.

### 3. Classes 9 to 12 or college: 300 words, three minutes

It takes three minutes at 100 words a minute, under two at the adult median, so seniors should slow down. It argues one idea.

> Respected Principal, teachers and friends, good morning. I have three minutes, so I will spend them on one small object: the clay diya.

> On Friday, 29 October 2027, millions of these lamps will be lit across India and in homes far beyond it. Many are still shaped by hand, by a potter at a wheel, and dried in the sun. Before a diya holds any light, it is simply earth, water and fire.

> The first lesson is that light can be shared without being lost. When you tilt one flame to light the next, the first flame does not get smaller. Knowledge works the same way: a teacher who explains something to forty students does not know it any less, and a friend who shares notes before an exam loses nothing.

> The second lesson is about timing: Lakshmi Puja is held on amavasya, the new-moon night, the darkest night of the month. Our ancestors did not wait for an easy night to celebrate light. They chose the hardest one, which is worth remembering in a difficult exam week.

> The third lesson is that this lamp belongs to many traditions. For many Hindu families it welcomes Lord Rama home to Ayodhya and invites Goddess Lakshmi in. Jain families light it for Mahavira's final liberation, and Sikh families for Bandi Chhor Divas, the homecoming of the sixth Guru Hargobind from Gwalior Fort.

> So here is my request for this Diwali. Buy a few diyas from a potter near your home, so the hands that made them share the festival too. Light one for a neighbour who lives alone, and keep the evening calm for the dogs on our street.

> One small flame can light a hundred others. Let us each be that flame this year, at home. Happy Diwali, and thank you.

## A short Diwali speech in Hindi, about 25 seconds

This 40-word speech takes about 25 seconds. A transliteration and gloss follow.

> आदरणीय प्रधानाचार्य जी, शिक्षकगण और प्यारे साथियों, सुप्रभात। इस वर्ष दीपावली शुक्रवार, 29 अक्टूबर 2027 को है।

> एक दीया दूसरे दीये को जलाता है, फिर भी उसकी लौ कम नहीं होती। ख़ुशी भी बाँटने से बढ़ती है। शुभ दीपावली, धन्यवाद।

*Transliteration:* Aadarniya pradhanacharya ji, shikshakgan aur pyaare saathiyon, suprabhaat. Is varsh Deepavali Shukravaar, 29 October 2027 ko hai.

Ek diya doosre diye ko jalaata hai, phir bhi uski lau kam nahin hoti. Khushi bhi baantne se badhti hai. Shubh Deepavali, dhanyavaad.

*English gloss:* Respected Principal, teachers and dear friends, good morning. This year Deepavali is on Friday, 29 October 2027.

One lamp lights another, yet its own flame does not shrink. Happiness, too, grows when shared. Happy Deepavali, thank you.

## Diwali 2027 dates a speech can safely quote

Every date above was checked against the [Drik Panchang Diwali 2027 calendar](https://www.drikpanchang.com/diwali/diwali-puja-calendar.html?year=2027) on 22 October 2026. Dhanteras is Wednesday 27 October, Choti Diwali Thursday 28, Lakshmi Puja Friday 29, Govardhan Puja Saturday 30 and Bhai Dooj Sunday 31 October 2027.

Tamil Deepavali comes a day sooner in Drik Panchang, on Thursday, 28 October 2027. In Tamil Nadu, use the school's own calendar.

## Word count and speaking time, compared

This converts each text into stage time at a child's pace and the adult median, with SubhSandesh's letter length as a yardstick.

| Text | Words | At 100 words a minute | At 162 words a minute |
|---|---|---|---|
| Classes 1–4 speech (English) | 100 | 60 seconds | 37 seconds |
| Classes 5–8 speech (English) | 200 | 2 minutes | 74 seconds |
| Classes 9–12 speech (English) | 300 | 3 minutes | 111 seconds |
| Hindi speech | 40 | 24 seconds | 15 seconds |
| SubhSandesh miss-you letter, median (n = 214) | 88 | 53 seconds | 33 seconds |

A speech written at an adult's pace runs long for a Class 4 child, so time it once with a stopwatch. The Hindi row is rougher, because both studies measured English or Dutch.

## Delivery tips from research on children's stage fear

[Kahlon and colleagues (2019)](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC6933883) note that one in three people report anxiety when speaking before others, often fearing the mind going blank. In their trial, 27 adolescents aged 13 to 16 practised speeches before a virtual classroom for one 90-minute session, and their anxiety fell and stayed lower three months later.

In [Velthuizen and colleagues' 2026 study](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12832577), 41 socially anxious adolescents aged 11 to 17 gave a five-minute speech before and after 12 weeks of group therapy. Afterwards they looked at audience faces more often, but their ums and restarts did not change.

- **Practise before people, not a mirror.** Three run-throughs before family mirror what helped in 2019.
- **Write a cue card.** Note the first three words of each paragraph: four cues for one minute, seven for three.
- **Pick three friendly faces.** Left, centre and right; looking at faces is what changed in 2026.
- **Do not drill out every "um".** Twelve weeks of therapy did not shift them.
- **Rehearse two days early.** The Raksha Bandhan figures above show how late festival tasks slide.

Want a story instead? Our separate Diwali story post retells it for children.

## Where SubhSandesh fits after the assembly, and where it does not

SubhSandesh does not write or time speeches, and its Diwali page is not a speech tool. It suits one relative who missed the assembly, perhaps a grandparent in another city.

For that person, the [playable Diwali card from SubhSandesh](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-diwali) opens on a diya at their doorstep carrying your tag, then has them colour a rangoli until your initials appear and unseal a letter from a shagun liffafa. Making it takes roughly five minutes, it carries up to six photos and it needs no app; a phone opens 48.3% of shared SubhSandesh pages.

To let them hear your child's voice, the [Dedication radio-show page](https://subhsandesh.in/dedication) fits better. They find your station through static, then your recorded voice introduces a song.

- Kahlon, Lindner & Nordgreen, [VR exposure therapy for adolescents' fear of public speaking](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC6933883), Child and Adolescent Psychiatry and Mental Health, 27 December 2019.
- Velthuizen et al., [CBT and adolescents' behaviour during public speaking](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12832577), Research on Child and Adolescent Psychopathology, 26 January 2026.

structuralLimitations: The 100 words-a-minute basis is an editorial choice anchored on US oral reading fluency norms (unfamiliar text, US pupils) and a Dutch adult study; no open-access Indian norm was usable — the one found ('Clinical Use of the Kannada and English Rate of Reading Tests', PMC6764215) is in Frontiers in Psychology, banned by the BRIEF. The post tells readers to time the speech aloud.

Both anxiety studies are clinical or sub-clinical samples (27 adolescents in a non-randomised VR pilot; 41 adolescents with social anxiety disorder, no control group). The post presents them as pointers for practice, not as proof that these tips cure stage fear.

First-party data is tangential: no Diwali or speech data exists. The 88-word miss-you letter median (n = 214, template live since 2026-07-28) is used only as a length yardstick; the Raksha Bandhan lead-time line is labelled as the nearest festival analogue (n = 89).

Tamil Nadu: Drik Panchang lists Tamil Deepavali on Thu 28 Oct 2027. The BRIEF reports holiday sites listing 29 Oct; this writer did not verify those lists, so the post states Drik Panchang's date and tells Tamil Nadu readers to use the school calendar.
The '94-word two-minute sample' observation comes from the #1 result (Vedantu), counted 2026-10-22; it is stated in the body without naming or linking the competitor.

Sibling diwali-essay had not been written when this post was finalised (blogs/ checked 2026-10-22); overlap with it must be checked in Phase 8. Sibling diwali-story gets a one-line unlinked pointer, because the BRIEF bans /blog/ links.

Phase 8 remediation (2026-10-22): the speeches were regrouped by audience (Classes 1-4, 5-8, 9-12/college) with minutes as an attribute, so the H1 and H3s no longer copy the incumbents' minute-led grouping. Office or society-function variants were not added: the body sits at the 1,800-word ceiling and each new speech would need its own count and timing.

failed.item: At least one table column uses first-party data
failed.why: Structural. The table rows are speeches, and SubhSandesh holds no data on speeches or speaking time; the only first-party value is one yardstick row (median miss-you letter, 88 words, n = 214). facts.md was re-read in full on 2026-10-22: the nearest spoken-word line, 13.6% of miss-you senders recording a voice note (29 of 214), is a share of pages, not a per-row duration, so a column built from it would be invented. Re-check trigger: a read-only probe of recorded voice-note durations in seconds on /missyou-gf or /dedication, once at least ~100 recordings exist (29 on /missyou-gf as of 2026-09-25); a median spoken-message length would then become a real column beside the 100- and 162-word-a-minute columns.

auditReport.honestAssessment: Of the five pages analysed, none states how many words fit a minute or why; this post writes three original speeches to exact counts (recounted at 100, 200, 300 and 40 words) on a cited reading-rate basis, and now organises them by the speaker's class band, tying each length to that grade's oral-reading norm, where Vedantu and FirstCry organise by minutes alone. That gives an answer engine a citable figure for 'how many words is a 2 minute speech'. It will still not outrank Vedantu, FirstCry or BYJU'S on the head term soon: they hold far more authority, the reading norms are American and Dutch rather than Indian, and SubhSandesh's first-party data only frames the topic; no table column measures anything spoken.
